definition: The area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve, summarizing a classifier's ability to distinguish between classes across thresholds.
details: An AUC of 1.0 indicates perfect separability, while 0.5 indicates performance no better than random guessing.

explainer.lead: ROC-AUC is a single number summarizing how well a classifier separates two classes across all decision thresholds. It matters because it measures ranking quality without committing to one threshold.

tiers.eli5: Imagine sorting a mixed pile of red and blue balls: a score of 1.0 means every red comes before every blue, and 0.5 means you're sorting at random.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to compare classifiers and to tune for ranking rather than a fixed cutoff. A pitfall is reading it as calibration or as accuracy at the threshold you will actually deploy.
tiers.paperLevel: It is the area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve, which plots true positive rate against false positive rate as the threshold varies; 1.0 means perfect separability and 0.5 means performance no better than random guessing.

explainer.example: A model with AUC 0.5 is no better than guessing, while AUC 1.0 means it perfectly ranks positives above negatives.
